message.content: {"caption":"A four-stage WikiSkill workflow exchanges information with three persistent knowledge layers and loops back for another iteration.","description":"A process diagram has three horizontal rounded layers above four colored workflow boxes. The top gray layer is “Skill Layer (skills/)”: a folder icon denotes its evolving procedural knowledge, described as “Evolving Procedural Knowledge” and “(Reversible, Conditional Update).” The middle gray layer is “Wiki Layer (wiki/)”: a lightbulb over books denotes structured knowledge, labeled “Structured Patterns & Evolution Logs” and “(Compounding, Never Reset).” The bottom gray layer is “Raw Layer (raw/)”: a padlock denotes stored traces, labeled “Immutable Execution Traces” and “(Permanent, Write Once).”\n\nThe four workflow boxes run left to right. Blue “Step 1: Inference Agent,” with a robot icon, says “Execute Rollouts on the Training Set.” A blue downward arrow labeled “Inject Skills” carries skills from the Skill Layer to Step 1; a separate blue upward arrow labeled “Write Traces” carries traces from Step 1 to the Raw Layer. A blue horizontal arrow leads to coral “Step 2: Wiki Maintainer,” shown with a wrench/gear icon and labeled “Perform Root-Cause Analysis on Traces.” A downward red arrow labeled “Sample Traces” goes from the Raw Layer to Step 2, and an upward red arrow labeled “Consolidate Patterns” goes from Step 2 to the Wiki Layer. A red horizontal arrow leads to yellow “Step 3: Skill Proposer,” shown with a lightbulb icon and labeled “Propose Skill Updates from Wiki and Traces.” Three yellow downward arrows, grouped under “Read Skill, Wiki, Traces,” bring information from the Skill, Wiki, and Raw layers to Step 3. A yellow horizontal arrow leads to green “Step 4: Gating & Rollback,” with a checked box and a pink X icon, labeled “Evaluate Skill Candidate on the Validation Set.” From Step 4, a green upward arrow labeled “Update the Skill if Better” points to the Skill Layer, and another green upward arrow labeled “Update Wiki Logs” points to the Wiki Layer. Along the bottom, a green return path labeled “Next Iteration” runs from Step 4 leftward and then upward into Step 1.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
